- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 10–20% for low sentiment periods.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), especially in early forecast horizon — cap forecast at 1.2x the 14-day moving average after such spikes.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher prices in the 10–15 day horizon; apply downward correction of 5–15% for 10–15 day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Mean reversion is evident in 20–30 day forecasts: if forecast is >1.5x recent 14-day average, reduce by 20–30% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Model underestimates in low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤0.33) — increase forecast by 10–20% for 10–20 day horizons when sentiment is weak or negative.
